page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the n1 family. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The architecture is x86_64, supported by dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 360.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25 percent. Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block bandwidth reaching 3918.64 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 92.34 GB/sec, both in the top 25 percent. Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance at 62.03 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-standard-96 is its weak single-threaded execution and poor text generation speeds for language models, with small model text generation landing in the bottom 10 percent. However, its high memory bandwidth and strong multi-core capabilities make it highly suitable for parallelized workloads. It is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving, offering a balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise applications.
